page: Microsoft Azure HB368-288rs_v5 is a high-density compute-optimized server belonging to the HBv5 family. It features 288 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture with Intel processors, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system allocates 448.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.56 GB per core, which prioritizes raw parallel processing power over per-core memory capacity.

This server is equipped with a substantial local storage array consisting of 15851 GB of NVMe SSD storage. It is also designated as Premium Storage capable and RDMA capable, enabling high-throughput, low-latency networking and storage operations. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this instance.

The primary tradeoff of this hardware profile is the low memory density per core, which may limit its effectiveness for memory-bound workloads. However, the combination of 288 dedicated vCPUs, massive local NVMe SSD storage, and RDMA capabilities makes this server highly suitable for large-scale compute-intensive workloads, distributed databases, high-performance computing simulations, and parallel processing tasks that require fast local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure HB368-288rs_v5 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server from the HBv5 family, featuring 288 dedicated Intel vCPUs and 448.0 GB of system memory. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance provides a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.56 GB per core, optimizing resource density for highly parallelized computational tasks. It includes a massive 15851 GB local NVMe SSD storage array and supports both Premium Storage and RDMA networking. The lack of integrated GPUs and the low per-core memory allocation represent key architectural tradeoffs. This server is designed for high-performance computing, large-scale parallel processing, and intensive storage or database workloads that benefit from high-speed local storage and low-latency RDMA interconnects.
